stem: Events A and B are such that P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A and B) = 0.2. What is P(A | B)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Returning P(B) = 0.5, which would be P(B|A) applied incorrectly, or confusing the conditioning event.
Returning P(A and B) = 0.2 directly, forgetting to divide by P(B), treating joint probability as conditional probability.
Computing P(A and B) / P(A) = 0.2 / 0.4 = 0.5, then misidentifying this as P(B|A) = 0.5, but writing 0.8 = 1 - 0.2 erroneously using complement.

explanation: Conditional probability: P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B) = 0.2 / 0.5 = 0.40. This is the proportion of B's probability that is also shared with A.

explanation_sections.punchline: Conditional probability divides the joint by the probability of the given event (the denominator), not by the probability of A.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: direct conditional probability formula. Map givens: P(A and B) = 0.2, P(B) = 0.5 (the conditioning event). Apply P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B) = 0.2/0.5 = 0.4.
explanation_sections.lesson: P(A|B) = P(A intersect B) / P(B); the denominator is always the probability of the event you are conditioning on.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. One division. The trap is dividing by P(A) = 0.4 instead of P(B) = 0.5, giving P(B|A) = 0.5, which equals P(B) coincidentally here.
